requirements.evidence: config/services.php:40 adds 'mention_id' => env('DISCORD_MENTION_ID'); app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:87-105 mentionId() accepts int or string, trims, and requires preg_match('/^[0-9]{17,20}$/'), which rejects '@everyone', 'abc', '123' and "123\n@everyone" (the '$' trailing-newline quirk can't apply because trim() runs first); :71-78 with no mention the output is unchanged (mb_substr to 1800), with a mention it reserves mb_strlen($suffix) and appends "\n<@id>" on its own line, so the mention survives truncation and the total stays <= 1800; send() signature, no-op, redaction and logging paths are untouched; .env.example, devops.md and logging.md are all updated.

conventions.evidence: Conventions say 'No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test', but the diff has no test file. CHANGELOG.md is not updated under [Unreleased] even though the docs-in-sync rule requires it. The PHPDoc on the new mentionId() and the ops docs updates do follow conventions.

security.evidence: The strict snowflake allow-list at app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:101 (after trim at :99) blocks @everyone/@here and newline injection. Non-string, non-int config values return null (:94-96). The webhook URL handling and redaction are unchanged.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no Pest/PHPUnit tests. Nothing covers the valid mention, the null/empty/invalid values ('@everyone', '123', "123\n@everyone"), mention survival under truncation, or the unchanged 1800-char behavior without a mention.

simplicity.evidence: Small, direct change. It reuses formatContent() with an optional $mentionId parameter (:61), adds a single helper mentionId() (:87) and one regex, and builds no new abstractions.

readability.evidence: The names are clear ($base, $suffix, $candidate), the new method has a PHPDoc explaining why it validates (:79-85), and the style matches the sibling code (private helpers, `! ` negation, mb_* functions).

scope.evidence: Every touched file (.env.example, config/services.php, DiscordOpsAlert.php, docs/ops/devops.md, docs/ops/logging.md) serves the task. No unrelated edits.

issues.explanation: The new mention behavior ships without any Pest test (valid id, empty/null, injection values, truncation with mention, unchanged length without mention), which violates the project's mandatory TDD rule.
The new DISCORD_MENTION_ID feature is not recorded under [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md, which the docs-in-sync convention requires.
The default `= null` on the private formatContent() $mentionId parameter is unnecessary because the method's only caller always passes the argument.

review.summary: The change adds DISCORD_MENTION_ID / services.discord.mention_id, strictly validates it as a 17-20 digit snowflake, and appends `<@id>` on its own line. It reserves room for the mention when truncating, and it documents the setting in .env.example and the ops docs. The implementation is correct, safe and lean, but it ships with no tests (the project requires TDD) and does not update CHANGELOG.md, so it needs changes before merge.
